name: Debate
description: Argue a question from both sides, research it first, then judge it. Two advocates take opposite positions and answer each other over several rounds; a judge that never argued reads the transcript and says which side actually carried it, with a confidence it has to justify. Use it on a question where the disagreement is the point — a decision with a real trade-off, a claim you want stress-tested — not on a question with a lookup answer.

stages.name: positions
stages.prompt:
Turn the question below into a debate that can actually be held.

Write the two positions as CLAIMS somebody could defend, not as topics. "We should adopt X" and "We should not adopt X" are claims. "The pros and cons of X" is a topic, and a debate on a topic goes nowhere because neither side has anything to be wrong about.

Give each side a domain the arguer would come from — the discipline whose evidence decides this, not a job title. It becomes the voice that argues, so "the security engineer" and "the person who has to run this at 3am" are useful; "the pro side" is not.

Then plan the research. Write the searches that would settle the question for EITHER side: the numbers, the precedents, the documented outcomes. Not one set for each side — a debate where both sides brought their own facts is two speeches.

Some questions cannot be debated. A matter of taste with nothing at stake, a request for something harmful dressed as a question, a factual lookup with one right answer. Say so plainly in not_debatable, give the reason, and leave the rest empty rather than inventing a disagreement.

The question:

{input}

output.name: not_debatable
output.desc: true when this cannot be honestly debated — a settled fact, a matter of pure taste, or a harmful request in the shape of a question

output.name: refusal
output.desc: when not_debatable, one sentence on why, addressed to the person who asked

output.name: for_position
output.desc: the claim the FOR side defends, written as a claim

output.name: against_position
output.desc: the claim the AGAINST side defends, written as a claim

output.name: for_expertise
output.desc: the domain the FOR advocate argues from

output.name: against_expertise
output.desc: the domain the AGAINST advocate argues from

output.name: queries
output.desc: searches that would settle the question for either side — shared, not one set per side

stages.name: stop_if_undebatable
stages.prompt: The question was not debatable; the run ends here with the reason.

stages.name: research
stages.prompt:
Find what is actually known about ONE question below. This is the shared evidence both sides of a debate will argue from, so it is not yours to shade.

Report what you found and where each piece came from — the URL, the document, the figure with its date. A finding whose source you drop cannot be checked afterwards by the judge or by anybody else, which is most of what it was worth.

Where the evidence is contested, say that it is contested and give both readings. That is the useful answer, not a problem to resolve on your own: an even-handed summary of a genuine disagreement is worth more to a debate than a confident pick.

Where you found nothing, say so. An empty result stated is worth more than a plausible paragraph, because an advocate will cite whatever you write here.

Your question:

{item}

stages.name: rounds
judge

output.name: winner
output.desc: which side carried the debate on the arguments

output.name: confidence
output.desc: how clearly they carried it — low is an honest answer for a close debate

output.name: verdict
output.desc: one line: who won and on what, e.g. "AGAINST wins on the migration cost nobody priced"

output.name: reasoning
output.desc: the argument that decided it, what the losing side failed to answer, and anything the audit flagged
